thread:
Jordan: heads up — putting together a short customer-facing hardware sizing mini-guide for Private/VPC installs. POC asking for numbers for a 50 qps gen endpoint (streaming allowed), expected 95th-percentile burst x2 for EOW reports. any quick rules of thumb? :thinking:
Lee: baseline question — what model family are they planning to run? 7B/13B/70B make a big diff. also single-token latency SLO?
Jordan: they said 'mix of 13B quantized + a couple 70B for heavier flows', target p95 latency <= 300ms for small prompts, and throughput target is 50 concurrent qps sustained with bursts to 100 qps for ~15 minutes.
Sana: ok. quick thumb rules i use: for 13B int8 you can get ~20-40 qps per A100-80GB when using batching and KV cache depending on seq len. for 70B quant you need H100 or multi-GPU partitioning — often ~6-12 qps per GPU. network/storage and CPU matter too for batching pipelines.
Devon: also remember Private deployments often hit node density limits — plan for 10–15% headroom + a canary pool. so for sustained 50 qps of mixed traffic i'd suggest capacity for 70 qps as baseline, and burst headroom to 110.
Matt: +1. here's a tiny calc i dropped into the sizing sheet earlier:
```
Assumptions:
 - 13B int8 on A100: 30 qps per GPU
 - 70B int8 on H100: 8 qps per GPU
Traffic mix:
 - 70% of requests go to 13B, 30% to 70B
Needed qps capacity:
 - 13B demand = 0.7 * 70 = 49 qps -> 49/30 = 1.63 -> 2 A100 GPUs
 - 70B demand = 0.3 * 70 = 21 qps -> 21/8 = 2.63 -> 3 H100 GPUs
 Total GPUs = 5 (plus 1 canary + 15% headroom -> round to 7 GPUs)
```
Jordan: nice. also need to call out infra requirements: each GPU node should have at least 96–128 vCPUs for throughput and batching threads, 1.5–2TB NVMe for model shards/swap/cache depending on sharding strategy, and 25–50Gbps NIC to avoid network stalls for KV cache fetches.
Sana: for VPC installs we add: separate mgmt plane subnet, VPN peering bandwidth reservation, and at least 2x NAT gateways for HA. note customers often forget egress costs for telemetry/shipment to the control plane.
Devon: ops-bot: post current private sizing template link?
ops-bot: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-sizing-template :page_facing_up: (auto-posted)
Lee: one more practical note — plan GPU-hours for training/benchmarking: initial onboarding benchmarking takes ~24–48 GPU-hours per model variant. for this config expect ~200 GPU-hours of setup + 10–20 GPU-hours/month for routine evals per customer. include that in cost quotes.
Jordan: good call. and about seasonal demand — client flagged end-of-quarter report peaks and marketing promos. recommend we compute monthly demand forecasts using 95th-percentile weekly peaks and apply a seasonality multiplier (historical multiplier 1.25 for EOW, 1.5 for major launches).
Matt: ops suggestion: offer an optional burst pool (hosted) with automatic fallback to hosted endpoints for spikes above private capacity. gives customers a softer budget cap and avoids overprovisioning. need to ensure data residency rules are clear.
Sana: can we add a checklist in the guide for on-prem folks: power/cooling per rack (H100 draw), PDU redundancy, PCIe wiring for NVLink bridges, and KMS/HSM placement for keys? short bullets.
Jordan: yes. i'll draft the guide with: overview, quick calc examples, infra checklist, forecast methodology, recommended monitoring thresholds (GPU util 70% target, memory spill <5%), and billing template.
Devon: i can help with the monitoring thresholds and alert playbooks.
Jordan: thanks — i'll post a draft in #eng-infra for review tomorrow morning. cc @Sana @Lee @Matt :thumbsup:
Matt: :thumbsup:
Sana: :eyes: will review asap.
Jordan: action items: 1) Jordan to draft doc + paste into thread (due +24h). 2) Devon to provide alert thresholds + runbook snippets. 3) Matt to add burst-hosted fallback text and data residency notes. 4) Sana to add ops checklist.
Lee: sounds good. leaving a note to ops that we should flag network bandwidth and storage IOPS in quotes — those are usually hidden costs that bite customers.
Jordan: awesome. thanks team.
